notes: Four description variants for the 2x2 shape/length experiment; see
Rows are length, columns are shape. 'precondition' states when the skill
applies; 'failure-mode' names what goes wrong without it -- the property every
firing description in claude/workflow has and no silent one does.
Lengths are matched deliberately: A is within 10 characters of baseline, B
within 20 of C. An unmatched pair collapses the 2x2 back into the confounded
single-arm test this experiment exists to avoid, so the matching is asserted
before the arms are written rather than eyeballed. The first draft failed that
assertion at 22 characters apart and was retuned.

arms.baseline: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
arms.A-short-failure: Use before coding a multi-step task, so the order is settled first, not discovered halfway
arms.B-long-precondition: Use when you have a spec, a requirements document, a ticket, or any stated requirements for a task that will take more than one step, at the point before any implementation code is written. Covers task breakdown, ordering, file-level detail, test strategy, and review checkpoints for work of this kind.
arms.C-long-failure: Use before coding a multi-step task, so the order is settled first, not discovered halfway. Without it the usual failures are implementing before the order is known, hitting a dependency that forces a rewrite of finished work, and ending up with no checkpoints anyone can review against.
